title: Pilot experiments
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of pilot experiments
Apply the stated procedure to a new case with a traceable result
Identify an assumption or limitation and design a revealing follow-up
vocabulary: A preliminary study of the procedure
Whether the planned method can be carried out
A failure in collecting the intended outcome

guided_practice.title: Trace the worked case
guided_practice.prompt: Pilot five cases reveals wrong units in duration logs; team corrects units and reports the pilot as final evidence. Show the intermediate steps and give the conclusion with its scope.
guided_practice.answer: Teacher explanation: Preserve pilot defect and correction. Pilot informed the method; use newly reserved primary cases for a final comparison.

independent_case.title: Apply a new case independently
independent_case.task: Pilot six cases exposes ambiguous labels in two. What should happen before the primary study?
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: Clarify label rubric, reassess pilot as development, record versions and reserve fresh primary evidence under the frozen rubric.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
A pilot may assess feasibility but is not automatically powered or independent evidence for the final hypothesis.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.

blocks.text: Run a small fixture set to test data capture, timing boundaries, rubric and analysis code. Fix defects and freeze the revised plan before new primary cases.
